picture.credit: Daniel Rutter, NASA Ames Research Center (NASA image ACD20-0047)

simplifications: The picture is NASA's 2019 illustration of VIPER, so the shape follows that design, not the rover as finally built.
The picture shows one end and one side; the generator guessed the far end, the other side and the underside (it made the two ends and the two sides alike).
Thin parts (the mast, its spiral, the cross-arm and the drill) are rough.
The drill is lowered to the ground in the picture and hung about 5 cm below the wheels; its tip was flattened to the bottom of the wheels (finishing.flatten_below), so the rover stands on its wheels.

Scaled evenly to NASA's overall height of 2.5 m; width and length are measured from the shape. NASA's public page gives a 1.5 m by 1.5 m footprint and a 2024 NASA briefing gives 1.7 m by 1.7 m; the latter is shown beside our figures for comparison.
All colours, textures and markings removed; one plain grey material.

finishing.material: one neutral material; every texture, image, UV coordinate, per-vertex colour and original material removed
